PARSONS CHOSEN PRESIDENT AND FOUR
NEW EXECUTIVE COUNCIL MEMBERS
ELECTED AT ANNUAL MEETING
At the annual meeting of the Executive
Councfl of Psi Upsilon on October 8,
1962, Robert W. Parsons, Xi '22, was
elected president of the Councfl. Brother
Parsons succeeds Benjamin T. Burton, Chi
'21, who became a life member in recog
nition of his many years of service to the
Fraternity.
Four new members, one elected at the
120th Convention and three at this meet
ing, were installed. They are: Cesar J.
Bertheau, Epsilon '19, Maxwell L. Scott,
Pi '28, Edward S. Fries, Eta '45 and
Walter L. Marr, Epsilon Omega '56. They
succeed Edward T. Richards, Sr., Sigma
'27, who resigned and was elected an
honorary life member; George L. Brain,
Iota '20, who resigned; Frederick A.
Nichols, Omicron '29, who resigned; and
Brother Burton.
ROBERT W. PARSONS
Xi '22
Brother Parsons, a 1922 graduate of
Wesleyan University, retired as a vicepresident of the Bankers Trust Company
in 1960 to take the leadership of three
educational and charitable foundations.
Robert W. Parsons
He is president and trustee of the LilHa
Babbitt Hyde Foundation, the John Jay
and Eliza Jane Watson Foundation and
the Charles E. and Joy C. Pettinos Foun
dation.
As chairman and director of the Inter
continental Advisory Corporation, Ltd.,
Brother Parsons oversees the research work
for the United International Fund, which
is affiliated with the United Mutual Fund
Investment Trust, a one biUion doflar plus
mutual fund.
For the past ten years he has been
Chairman of the Board of Directors of
the Charles E. Pettinos Graphite Corp.,
which is one of the leading importers and
refiners of graphite in this country.
Since retirement from the Bankers
Trust Company he has been elected a
member of the Board of Trustees of the
New York University Medical Center, and
is Treasurer of the Center at the present
time, as well as Chairman of the Univer
sity Hospital Committee. This is a
very
exciting assignment, dealing widr many
problems, and necessitating a
great deal
of time and effort.
Since graduating from college Brother
Parsons has been active in various capac
ities for Wesleyan University, including
Chairman of the Alumni Fund Drive
(1939-41), Vice-chairman of the Alumni
Councfl (1941-43), Trustee of the College
from 1941-46 when he served as Chair
man of the Endowment Committee and
as a member of the Executive Committee.
He was re-elected Trustee of Wesleyan in
1957, served on the Finance Committee
of the Board of Trustees, and in 1960 was
elected Trustee Emeritus.
Among some of the other assignments
which he has attempted to carry out were
the following: 1941-51 he was Chairman
of the Memorial Gifts Committee in a
campaign to rebuild Overlook Hospital
in Summit, New Jersey, and served on the
Board of Trustees of that hospital from
1950-56 where one of his committee as
signments included the Finance Commit
tee. He is still a member of the Finance
Committee of Overlook Hospital, but no
longer a Trustee. From 1946-53 he was

120th National Convention of the Frater
nity from September 5 through September
7, 1962. Over 300 alumni participated in
the varied program which ranged from a
Gala Smoker, business sessions and lunch
eons at the University Heights Campus of
New York University to the annual Con
vention Banquet and Founders Day Cele
bration at the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel.
Under the leadership of Brother J. Rus
sell McShane, Delta '32, chairman, and
Brothers Theodore E. Reynolds, Delta '31
and Paul J. Hughes, Delta '34, co-chair
men, the Delta Brothers, alumni and un
dergraduates, once
again proved them
selves a
dynamic and energetic force with
in the Fraternity. Honorary chairmen
were. Dr. Orrin S. Wightman, Delta '95
and Frank E. Booth, Delta '11, for many
years president of the Delta Corporation.

Wednesday evening
proved to be a

spirited feat of endurance.

Canada.
